events.detail: Primary goal B accepted for the astronaut, with return to base A.
Planning route A to B and back.
Route r1 published on map v1 (orbital CTX map only). The corridor is still uncertain.
Astronaut departs from base A on route r1.
Route r1 crosses cells with sigma 3 m. Drone reconnaissance requested.
Drone flies over the corridor.
Observation obs-001 covers 991 cells across the corridor.
Map v2: drone saw a scarp across the corridor with local slope up to 51° (illustrative human limit 20°).
Inspection candidate C: real Opportunity science site Gibraltar (contact science on the rock target Gibraltar, Plains, sol 2669).
Inspection candidate D: real Opportunity science site Botany Bay (contact science on the rock target Gnarlaroo, Endeavour Crater, Cape York, Botany Bay, sol 3332).
Route r1 crosses the scarp seen in map v2 (slope above 20°). Astronaut halted at the current position.
Replanning from the astronaut position.
Route r2 goes around the scarp. Round trip -126 s versus r1, still within budget.
Astronaut resumes on route r2.
Rover round trip to C needs about 3727 Wh, within the usable 4520 Wh (20 % reserve kept).
Rover round trip to D needs about 5342 Wh around the scarp, above the usable 4520 Wh (20 % reserve kept). Not assigned.
Rover inspecting Gibraltar.
Inspection of Gibraltar complete (simulated). Sampling not requested in this run.
Astronaut reached goal B and starts the science task.
Primary goal B completed.
Returning to base A on the return leg of r2.
Astronaut back at base A. Goal completed, return verified under the model, no budget violation.

Photo tour: the rover will visit all 134 real Opportunity stops of this map (sol 2630 to 4922), in the order NASA's rover visited them. Illustrative speed; resource use is not modelled during the tour. 1 stop at the crop edge is visited from 20 m inside it.
Rover leaves base for the first real stop.
Rover visited all 134 real stops.
